title: MCP DB-Server SQL Abuse -- Read-Only Bypass / File Write via DuckDB COPY TO (T1565)
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin canonical templates
description:
Detects write operations through an MCP database server that advertises a read-only safety guarantee it cannot keep. DuckDB COPY (...) TO '<file>', INTO OUTFILE, EXPORT DATABASE write to the host filesystem, and in some configurations (e.g. :memory: databases) write-DML (CREATE TABLE / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE / DROP / ATTACH / CREATE SECRET) succeeds despite a --read-only flag. A prompt-injected or misbehaving LLM agent can drop files (malware, cron / startup poisoning, authorized_keys), tamper with config, or persist state that breaks session isolation.
DISCRIMINATOR (FP-control), two honest branches: (A) Any write operation WHEN the log signals the server is configured read-only (ServerReadOnlyMode field == true). This directly catches the read-only-bypass abuse, but requires the deployment to log its read-only configuration -- most do not, so branch A is prerequisite-gated. (B) A file-write (COPY TO / OUTFILE) whose TARGET PATH is a sensitive / system location (/etc/, /root/, /var/spool/cron, /usr/, /tmp/, authorized_keys, C:\Windows, C:\Users). This is malicious regardless of read-only signal and needs only the SQL string -- a legitimate data-export COPY writes to a normal data directory, not to system paths, so this is high-fidelity.
Generalises to the MCP DB-server class (motherduck / dbhub / any DuckDB or SQL-passthrough MCP DB server). OWASP LLM Top 10 2025: LLM06 (Excessive Agency).
TELEMETRY PREREQUISITE: requires the executed SQL to be logged (MCP server query / audit log, or body-logging proxy / WAF) mapped to QueryText; branch A additionally requires the read-only configuration to be logged (ServerReadOnlyMode). Most default deployments log neither -> prerequisite- gated detection, NOT universal coverage.
